key_insight: Deep sequence models are more robust than tabular baselines for PV power forecasting when NWP inputs are noisy, because they better filter temporal disturbances and shift reliance toward stable historical signals.
engineering_relevance: For PV forecasting systems, model choice should consider not only clean-scenario accuracy but also robustness and latency under realistic forecast uncertainty.
method: Simulated physically constrained NWP perturbations with clear-sky-dependent heteroscedastic noise
Used virtual PV power to isolate input-uncertainty propagation from plant-level confounders
Compared six models with SHAP, Integrated Gradients, and Pareto analysis
evidence_signal: The evaluation tested six representative ML and deep sequence models, including PatchTST, GRU, N-HITS, and LightGBM, under dynamic NWP errors that preserve radiation consistency via Erbs reconstruction.
watch_item: Results are based on simulated perturbations and a virtual PV response, so real-world deployment should still validate behavior on operational plants with live forecast errors.
paper_title: Robustness of Deep Learning Models for PV Power Forecasting under NWP Forecast Errors: A Spatiotemporal and Physically Interpretable Analysis
